reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that tensile-compression asymmetry increases with Cu content and temperature in FeNiCrCoCu, but it is a molecular dynamics study at the nanoscale, not an experimental wear study. It does not address nano-twinning mechanisms, coating–substrate interface effects, or the link between asymmetry and wear, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Cu content increases tensile-compression asymmetry in FeNiCrCoCu
Nano-twinning is promoted during compression and dislocation slip reduced during tension at high Cu content
Tensile-compression asymmetry causes strain localization and stress concentration at the coating–substrate interface
Reducing Cu content leads to more uniform plastic deformation and less wear
